ambiguities.impact: A contract may assert existence and the printed certificates, but should not attribute an explicit uniqueness theorem or algorithm for recovering delta to the passage.

ambiguities.impact: The fictional backward perturbation must not be identified with actual representational rounding without an additional assumption.

ambiguities.evidence: Both certificates append O(epsilon^2) without defining its norm scaling or dependence on N, gamma, the radix factorization, or x. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: two unnumbered delta bounds)

ambiguities.impact: That sentence is a practical heuristic, not an additional precise norm theorem.

contract_plain_english: Every exact N-vector output roundoff error can be represented as the exact unnormalized Fourier transform of a hypothetical input perturbation. That perturbation has RMS norm equal to the output-error RMS norm divided by sqrt(N), and the paper gives first-order RMS and maximum-norm certificates in terms of epsilon, K(N,gamma), and ||x||_RMS. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: e=T delta and the two following bounds)

source_evidence.observation: The paper defines the unnormalized Nth-order complex Fourier matrix T by T(j,k)=exp(i2pi jk/N), writes y=Tx, and factors T into permutation, block-Fourier, and diagonal twiddle-factor matrices for the FFT.

source_evidence.anchor: floating-point and trigonometric models followed by Theorem 1
source_evidence.observation: The paper specifies epsilon and gamma error models and gives the one-dimensional RMS and maximum roundoff bounds with K(N,gamma).

The paper says the preceding analysis assumed exactly representable input, distinguishes actual input rounding fl(x)=x+delta from the later reverse use of the roundoff bounds, and introduces the limited-input-accuracy motivation.

source_evidence.anchor: prose assertion e=T delta and the two following unnumbered bounds
source_evidence.observation: For the exact complex N-vector roundoff error e, the paper asserts that e=T delta for some fictional delta and states ||delta||_RMS=||e||_RMS/sqrt(N)<=epsilon K(N,gamma)||x||_RMS+O(epsilon^2) and ||delta||_infinity<=epsilon sqrt(N)K(N,gamma)||x||_RMS+O(epsilon^2).

statement.algorithm_linkage: The certificates inherit Theorem 1's one-dimensional mixed-radix floating-point FFT and its K(N,gamma). The factorization is stated to apply to Cooley-Tukey and Sande-Tukey variants with different diagonal matrices and includes separate diagonal twiddle multiplications. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: equation (2.2) and following remarks; PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor: Theorem 1 and note following K)
binders: N is the transform order; x, e, and the fictional delta are complex N-vectors; e is the exact roundoff-error vector. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: opening prose of the fictional-perturbation passage)
T is the N-by-N unnormalized Fourier matrix with T(j,k)=exp(i2pi jk/N), j,k=0,...,N-1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: equation (2.1) and definition of T)

For K(N,gamma), N has an FFT factorization N=N_1...N_M, epsilon is the arithmetic error constant, and gamma is the absolute trigonometric-error constant. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor: numerical model and Theorem 1)
conclusions: There exists some fictional complex N-vector delta satisfying the exact equation e=T delta. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: prose assertion e=T delta)
||delta||_RMS = ||e||_RMS/sqrt(N) <= epsilon K(N,gamma)||x||_RMS + O(epsilon^2). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: first unnumbered delta bound)
||delta||_infinity <= epsilon sqrt(N)K(N,gamma)||x||_RMS + O(epsilon^2). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: second unnumbered delta bound)
constants_and_indexing: K(N,gamma)=sum_{l=1}^M alpha(N_l)+(M-1)(3+2gamma), with N=N_1...N_M, alpha(2)=sqrt(2), alpha(4)=5, and alpha(q)=2sqrt(q)(q+gamma) otherwise. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor: Theorem 1 definition of K and alpha)

The Fourier indices run from 0 to N-1, and the first norm equality uses exactly sqrt(N), not N or an index-shifted dimension. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: definition of T; PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: first delta bound)
definitions_and_conventions: The equation e=T delta represents the output roundoff error as the exact Fourier transform of a hypothetical input perturbation; the paper does not identify delta with a perturbation actually supplied to the machine. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: phrase 'some fictional delta')
||z||_RMS=((sum_{k=0}^{N-1}|z(k)|^2)/N)^(1/2) and ||z||_infinity=max_k |z(k)|. (PDF p. 1, printed p. 757, anchor: norm definitions)

T is unnormalized, so the selected passage uses the exact scaling ||T delta||_RMS=sqrt(N)||delta||_RMS. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: definition of T; PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: equality ||delta||_RMS=||e||_RMS/sqrt(N))
error_notions: e is forward output roundoff error, whereas delta is a fictional input perturbation furnishing a normwise backward-error interpretation. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: e=T delta and the two bounds)

The certificates are absolute RMS and infinity-norm bounds scaled by ||x||_RMS; they are not componentwise relative bounds on delta(k)/x(k). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: two unnumbered delta bounds)
exceptional_values: No overflow, underflow, subnormal, NaN, infinity, or failed-trigonometric-evaluation assumptions are stated in the passage or arithmetic model. (PDF pp. 2-3, printed pp. 758-759, anchor: equations (3.1)-(3.2) and trigonometric model; PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: fictional-delta passage)
higher_order_terms: The equation e=T delta and the norm equality are exact; only the two upper estimates carry additive O(epsilon^2) remainders. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: e=T delta and the two bounds)
The source does not state the constants, parameter dependence, or uniformity hidden in O(epsilon^2). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: two unnumbered delta bounds)
hypotheses: The vector e is the roundoff error produced in the paper's one-dimensional floating-point FFT analysis, whose standing input assumption is fl(x)=x. (PDF p. 5, printed p. 761, anchor: proof preceding equation (3.6); PDF p. 9, printed p. 765, anchor: Section 6 input-representation discussion)
The exact transform is y=Tx and the roundoff analysis supplies the Theorem 1 bounds for e=fl(y)-y. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: equation (2.1); PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor: Theorem 1)

The reverse interpretation is introduced for input data known to fewer significant digits than machine precision; delta in the selected passage is expressly fictional. (PDF p. 9, printed p. 765, anchor: final paragraph; PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: fictional-delta prose)
implicit_context: Because y=Tx and e=fl(y)-y, e=T delta permits the inferred backward-error identity fl(y)=T(x+delta), although that latter equation is not itself printed in the selected passage. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: equation (2.1); PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: e=T delta)

The paper follows the bounds with a qualitative criterion: if epsilon sqrt(N)K(N,gamma)||x||_RMS is smaller than the least significant digit of the input data, the roundoff error is called negligible. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: sentence following the two delta bounds)
norms: The first certificate includes the exact equality ||delta||_RMS=||e||_RMS/sqrt(N). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: first unnumbered delta bound)
The second certificate controls max_k |delta(k)| and contains an additional sqrt(N) relative to the RMS certificate. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: second unnumbered delta bound)
numerical_model: The arithmetic model is fl(a+b)=a(1+theta epsilon)+b(1+theta epsilon) and fl(ab)=ab(1+theta epsilon), with independently varying theta in [-1,1]. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: equations (3.1)-(3.2))

With at least t+1 accumulation digits, epsilon is 0.5 beta^(1-t) for rounded operations and beta^(1-t) for chopped operations; with only t accumulation digits, the paper gives 0.5(1+1/beta)beta^(1-t) and (1+1/beta)beta^(1-t), respectively. (PDF pp. 2-3, printed pp. 758-759, anchor: paragraph defining epsilon)

The sine-and-cosine model is absolute: fl(sin(fl(a)))=sin(a)+gamma theta epsilon and fl(cos(fl(a)))=cos(a)+gamma theta epsilon, where gamma>=0 depends on their computation for the transform order but is independent of input data. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 759, anchor: trigonometric error model)

undebatable_constraints: The relation e=T delta is exact and delta is explicitly fictional. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: opening prose and equation e=T delta)
The RMS certificate contains both an equality and an upper bound; neither may be omitted. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: first unnumbered delta bound)
The infinity certificate is ||delta||_infinity<=epsilon sqrt(N)K(N,gamma)||x||_RMS+O(epsilon^2). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: second unnumbered delta bound)
Both certificates are normwise and scale with the exact input RMS norm, not the output norm or individual input components. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 768, anchor: two unnumbered delta bounds)
The transform T uses the paper's positive-sign, unnormalized complex Fourier convention. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 758, anchor: equation (2.1) and definition of T)
